advances: A continuous choice of which endpoint pays at each normal, with the middle erosion held fixed.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Use d90ba05577427854 to choose $a$. The tangent continuation is positive and decreasing as well as convex because its lower part has the constant negative derivative of the join and its upper part is a positive inverse power. Each field is jointly continuous and nonnegative and convex in the physical point for each fixed $n$. For each body use the singleton version of 84cd8a85417b0d7a with one ceiling equal to its original support. The middle gauge erosion corresponds to the field $H(n)f(1+a\cdot(x-y))$. This gives positivity and nesting for small parameters, including zero input fields on subsets of the sphere.

For old inputs $x\in A$, $x'\in B$ with $m=(x+x')/2$, the minima of the partner affine coordinates and monotonicity of $f$ give both $U_A(n,x)\ge2H(n)f(1+a\cdot(m-y))$ and the same bound for $U_B(n,x')$. For two eroded inputs add their cuts and divide by two. The normal-wise coefficients sum to one, so $n\cdot m+\varepsilon H(n)f(1+a\cdot(m-y))\le(h_A(n)+h_B(n))/2\le h_K(n)$. This is exactly the target gauge inequality for all $n$. As only the middle midpoint needs to be checked on $-1,0,1$, the lifted hull has those precise fibers.
statement:
Let $A,B,K$ be positive convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$, and choose $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $a$ be the positive projective centering parameter for $K-y$, and $f$ the positive decreasing convex inverse-power tangent extension at its minimum denominator. Put $H(n)=h_{K-y}(n)$ and choose $b_*\in B$ minimizing $a\cdot b$ and $a_*\in A$ minimizing $a\cdot x$. Define
$$
U_A(n,x)=2H(n)f(1+a\cdot((x+b_*)/2-y)),\qquad
U_B(n,x')=2H(n)f(1+a\cdot((a_*+x')/2-y)).
$$
For any continuous $t:\mathbb S^{d-1}\to[0,1]$, impose support erosions on $A,B$ using the fields $t(n)U_A(n,x)$ and $(1-t(n))U_B(n,x')$, and on $K$ use its projective gauge cut about $y$. The eroded bodies are nested and positive for small $\varepsilon\ge0$ and obey exact midpoint compatibility, giving actual integer fibers at $-1,0,1$.
title: Exact normal-dependent endpoint allocation for projective erosion
